predecessors.name: Ptolemaic Kingdom
predecessors.text: Thebes, which Harsiesi 'captured in the summer of 131 BC', and the south of Upper Egypt

successors.name: Ptolemaic Kingdom
successors.text: Thebes recaptured by Ptolemy's forces 'in November of the same year' and the southern Upper Egypt after Harsiesi's death, 'likely September 130 BC'

ledger.x: 131 BCE: Harsiesi seizes Thebes and takes pharaonic titles.
131 BCE: Thebes passes from the Ptolemaic kingdom to the rebel, in the civil war of Ptolemy VIII and Cleopatra II.
130 BCE: the rump of the rebel state ends with Harsiesi's death, 'likely' in September 130 BC.
130 BCE: Harsiesi dies, 'which likely occurred in September 130 BC'.

wars.name: Revolt of Harsiesi
wars.outcome: Harsiesi took Thebes in the summer of 131 and 'ruled only in the southern part of Upper Egypt and only for a brief period'; Ptolemy's forces recaptured the city in November; he died 'likely' in September 130.

certainty.note: The extent of the rebel state is the southern Upper Egypt of the page; no frontier is given.
